title: Small-batch Garage Lab: KV Sampler & Kernel Tuning (weekly scratches)
content:
Weekly lab scratches for the small-batch garage: focus this week was reducing variance on sub-8-token requests while keeping throughput steady. quick notes, experiments and action items below.

Meeting: Small-Batch Garage Lab sync
Date: 2026-09-22 (primary writeup)
Attendees: Aisha, Ben, Lina, Omar, Priya (brief)
Duration: 45m (standup + demo)
Purpose: triage last week's regressions on sampler-rate jitter, test micro-kernel path for sub-16 sequences, and decide rollout gating for the new coalesce heuristic.

Agenda:
- Show recent p95 surge on low-token chat (observed 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-21)
- Walk through sampler instrumentation and new counters
- Review micro-kernel patch (PR 729) perf numbers on dev-rig
- Decide immediate mitigations for customer-facing instability windows
- Assign follow-ups + sketches for next experiments

Observed problem summary:
- On 2026-09-20 at ~03:00 UTC we saw repeated p95 spikes for requests with <8 tokens. Not peak throughput, but variance (jitter) increased from baseline 14ms -> 90ms bursts for a subset of traffic.
- Root suspects: sampler under-sampling leading to small, unfilled batches + kernel path switching thrash when selector toggles between micro and baseline kernels mid-run.
- Secondary: new coalescer heuristic (opt-in on canary) increases batch tail latency for particular routing hash ranges.

Quick instrumentation findings (new fields added):
- sampler.fill_attempts: how many attempts to push request into sample window before giving up (new counter)
- kernel_switch_count: increments when runtime switches kernel mid-inference
- small_batch_wait_ms: observed waits introduced by coalescer for tiny requests
- result: places with high sampler.fill_attempts correlate strongly with jitter windows.

Experiments run this week:
1) Micro-kernel warm path (PR 729) on dev-rig (2x A100):
   - baseline: p95 small-requests 78ms, throughput 1200 req/s
   - patch: p95 reduced to 44ms when kernel sticky is enabled; sticky flag prevents mid-request kernel switching
   - note: throughput unchanged, but CPU spike on sidecar when sticky true (ben to profile)

2) Sampler backoff tuning (A/B):
   - A: aggressive 10ms greedy fill (current) -> higher fill_attempts, occasional starvation of larger batches
   - B: linear 20ms backoff with max 60ms -> fewer kernel switches, slightly higher average latency but lower p95
   - result: B reduced p95 jitter by ~35% on synthetic replay, recommended for canary fallback

3) Coalescer routing tweak: avoid delaying requests with <6 tokens for the coalesce window (sketch only)
   - early results show reduced small-request tail but small throughput loss at peak due to less batching; trade-off acceptable for hosting tier SLA

Demo highlights:
- Lina replayed the 90ms spike trace and showed kernel_switch_count jumping from 0->3 within a single request lifecycle; sticky kernel eliminates those jumps.
- Omar showed heatmap of sampler.fill_attempts by route; two customer routes dominated the noise (sha: ab12/route-catalog)

Decisions taken:
- Immediate rollback plan for coalescer heuristic on canary: disable for hosting tier during next 24h window if repeat spike occurs (owner: Ben)
- Promote micro-kernel sticky flag to canary-forced on dev region for 48h (owner: Aisha + Ben)
- Adopt backoff-B sampler config for one customer cohort (SERVE-3304) as an experiment (owner: Priya)

Action items (short):
- Aisha: merge observability patch that surfaces kernel_switch_count to main metrics pipeline (ticket: SERVE-3281). target: 2026-09-24.
- Ben: profile sidecar CPU with sticky kernel enabled; capture flame graphs and note hotspots. target: 2026-09-24.
- Lina: prepare replay for customer route ab12 with 2x larger sampling window; measure small-request tail impact. target: 2026-09-25.
- Omar: roll back coalescer heuristic on canary and coordinate with infra for quick toggles. target: immediate/ASAP.
- Priya: patch deployment plan for sampler backoff-B to cohort of customers, write up canary gating in Confluence page. target: 2026-09-27.

Open questions / discussion notes:
- What is acceptable trade-off for canary vs hosting? early feedback: hosting SLA favors tail latency over pure throughput; we should opt to reduce p95 at small cost in throughput for hosting tier.
- Is sticky kernel sticky forever? we need a smarter affinity that respects thermal/throughput signals; longer-term sketch: sticky-per-request TTL + server-level health signal.
- Could sampler oversampling help warm KV caches? Maybe prefetch hint on large cohorts; sketch for next week.

Ideas to explore (backlog):
- sampler-aware KV prefill: if route historically small tokens, pre-warm small KV slots before request arrives
- hybrid coalescer: dynamic window that shortens for high variance routes and lengthens for stable ones
- kernel affinity map persisted across short TTLs so subsequent requests reuse same kernel selection (reduce switch thrash)

Metrics snapshot (dev-rig baseline vs experiment):
- baseline dev-rig small-req p95: 78ms -> experiment sticky kernel 44ms (improvement 44%)
- sampler.fill_attempts avg: baseline 2.8 -> backoff-B 1.1 on synthetic replay
- throughput: unchanged within noise +/-3% on test harness

Notes-to-self (informal):
- keep canary toggles obvious and under hands-on deck when altering coalescer that touches routing hash ranges.
- remember to add a short note in customer-facing incident runbook about small-batch jitter (so ops knows to flip sampler config).
- re-check PR 729 for any hidden memory churn when sticky enabled; watch nvml mem usage during long runs.

Next sync: 2026-09-29 (same time). plan: report sidecar profile, merge metrics patch, and get first cohort deployment telemetry.
